status_vocabulary.verified: reproduced under stated conditions with a public receipt
status_vocabulary.measured: one or more runs, receipt public in this repo
status_vocabulary.measured-private: the run happened and the receipt exists, but only in a private audit tree -- a reader of this repo cannot check it
status_vocabulary.retired: was published, now known wrong; kept so the retraction is findable
status_vocabulary.superseded: true as measured, but a later entry is the number to quote
status_vocabulary.open: a question the docs raise with no evidence either way

claims.claim: Single-stream (B=1) paged decode of Qwen3-30B-A3B with NF4 experts and the fp8 paged KV cache runs at roughly 100 tok/s on a rented RTX 5090.
claims.hardware: RTX 5090 (sm_120), rented Vast.ai host; the 5090 class carries ~8.5% inter-box dispersion
claims.conditions: B=1, NF4 experts, fp8 paged KV (k_groups=4), 512-token prompt, graph-timed, --no-fuse-qkv, e4b 0.30.0 stack
claims.notes: Same-box NF4 baseline; the earlier public rungs (bench/hybrid-g9/f1, bv2) put the NF4 single stream at 94-134 tok/s on the same class as the glue rounds landed.

claims.claim: With calibrated int4 attention (E4B_SERVE_ATTN_INT4_CALIB=1) and int4 experts, Qwen3-30B-A3B single-stream decode reaches 204.6 tok/s on the same 5090 class, x1.93 over the NF4 baseline.
claims.hardware: RTX 5090 (sm_120), rented
claims.conditions: B=1, int4-b32 experts + C4-calibrated int4 attention + glue rounds 1-3, K8 gate PASS (-0.042 ppl wikitext, -0.115 C4)
claims.notes: Qwen3-specific: the same lane is REFUSED on quality on Mixtral (+0.09) and OLMoE (+0.60). Not a general lever.

claims.claim: Batched (B=16) decode of Qwen3-30B-A3B with int4 experts reaches about 1,238 tok/s aggregate on a 5090, x2.50 over the NF4 batched baseline of about 490.
claims.hardware: RTX 5090 (sm_120), rented
claims.conditions: B=16, natural distinct prompts, int4 experts, graph replay, glue rounds 1-3
claims.notes: int4 attention is a B=1 lever only (x0.897 at B=16); rows>1 use cached bf16 attention weights.

claims.claim: On the same 5090, vLLM serving Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 is ahead of this stack by x1.47 at B=1 and x1.55 at B=16 with natural distinct prompts (1,917 vs 1,234 tok/s aggregate).
claims.hardware: RTX 5090, one box, both engines
claims.conditions: slope method (32->128 tokens) isolates decode; identical distinct prompts per row; template prompts had inflated vLLM by 13%, identical prompts by 2.8x
claims.notes: The only same-box, same-prompt comparison against a production engine this project has. Supersedes the 2026-08 '6.31x ahead' figure, which used template prompts and a different box.

claims.claim: Granite-3.1-3B-A800M's paged decode is indistinguishable from the model's own attention: 0.00229 nats from a chunk-free full-forward reference, below the model's own 0.00330-nat arithmetic-order floor.
claims.hardware: RTX 5090, rented
claims.conditions: 512 scored steps, 256-token prompt, wikitext-2 test, sha-matched ids across all three arms; NF4 experts on every arm
claims.notes: The serving path lands CLOSER to the chunk-free reference than the chunked production oracle does (0.00229 vs 0.00330).

claims.claim: gpt-oss-20b's paged decode (sinks + alternating sliding windows) is indistinguishable from the model's own attention: 0.00288 nats from a chunk-free full-forward reference, below its 0.01758-nat floor.
claims.hardware: RTX 5090, rented
claims.conditions: 512 scored steps, 256-token prompt, raw wikitext (out of distribution for this model; the DELTA is regime-independent), NF4 experts on every arm
claims.notes: Established on a 512-step window only; a full forward is quadratic in the window and cannot be run at 8192. The 8192-step +0.078 nats against a CHUNKED oracle is not evidence about the path (see the retired entry).

claims.claim: Qwen3-30B-A3B's paged decode is indistinguishable from the model's own attention: 0.00173 nats from a chunk-free full-forward reference, below the model's own 0.00641-nat arithmetic-order floor (512-step window). Its 8192-step delta against the chunked oracle (+0.0058 nats) also sits below the 8192-window floor of 0.0095.
claims.hardware: RTX 5090, rented
claims.notes: The serving path lands CLOSER to the chunk-free reference than the chunked production oracle does (0.00173 vs 0.00641). Third family with that ordering.
claims.conditions: 512 scored steps, 256-token prompt, wikitext-2 test, sha-matched ids across all three arms; NF4 experts on every arm; mech tally fp8

claims.claim: Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it's paged decode, serving two KV geometries from one pool with sliding windows and scale 1.0, agrees with the chunked oracle to -0.0078 nats over 8192 steps and produces coherent text; the absolute |dppl|<=0.05 bar is inapplicable at oracle ppl 752.
claims.hardware: RTX 5090 (188 GB RAM host), rented
claims.notes: Whole window ran the fp8 compute path (mech tally fp8 245760 / f32 0). Loading FAILS on 2 of 4 rented hosts (e4b#344, unexplained). SUPERSEDED 2026-09-03: this compared the paged path to the CHUNKED ORACLE, not to the model; against a chunk-free reference the path fails (see e4b.parity.gemma4.chunk-free).

claims.claim: Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it's paged decode is NOT at parity with the model's own attention: 0.24747 nats from a chunk-free full-forward reference on a 512-step window, 3.0x the model's own arithmetic-order floor (0.08137 nats, itself 5-25x any other family's). Cause open (e4b#359).
claims.hardware: RTX 5090, rented (Vast box 49779056)
claims.notes: full 3.34492 / chunked 3.42629 / paged 3.59239 nats. Two unexplained facts: the floor (HF chunked vs HF full) is 0.081 where other families sit at 0.003-0.018, and the paged gap changes SIGN between this window and the 8192-step window (ppl 28 vs 752). First test: the paged arm with a bf16 KV cache or finer fp8 K groups on this exact window (k_groups=4 at head_dim 512 = 128-wide scale groups). SUPERSEDED 2026-09-03 (P27): one window, one reference; three windows and the three-forward test show the model has no reference at this resolution.
claims.conditions: 512 scored steps, 256-token prompt, wikitext-2 test, sha-matched ids e01de6ebd4af across all three arms; NF4 experts on every arm; paged arm mech tally fp8 15360 / f32 0

claims.claim: Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it has no parity reference at 512-token resolution: the paged path is +0.093/+0.114/+0.247 nats from a one-shot forward on three windows while transformers' own cached forward is -0.107/+0.271/+0.081 from the same one-shot forwards; in plain transformers the NLL of identical prefix tokens moves 0.4 nats with the batch shape.
claims.hardware: RTX 5090, rented (Vast box 49785896)
claims.notes: Cache flag is a bit-exact no-op (cached prefill == short forward). Real vs random continuation moves prefix positions 0.24% at layer 1 -> 34% at layer 19 (bf16 batch-shape variance in the expert gathers, amplified by the router); Qwen3-30B: 0.15% -> 3.5%, NLL 0.001. Running the router in fp32 (plain transformers) does not remove the amplification (layer-19 divergence 0.25 against 0.34, top layer unchanged) and itself moves the same tokens' NLL by 1.1 nats, so router precision is not a lever; the sensitivity is the model's.
claims.conditions: 512 scored steps, 256-token prompt, wikitext-2 test, prompt offsets 0/3000/6000; NF4 experts on the e4b arms; plain bf16 transformers 5.16.1 for the three-forward test

claims.claim: The fp8 paged cache and fp8 dot cost Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it 0.046 nats on the P26b window (the kernel's full precision model -- Q per-tile, K 4-group, V per-row, P range-folded e4m3 -- applied inside the one-shot forward on the scored rows); 0.017 with 32-wide K groups; the five 512-dim full-attention layers carry 0.019 of it and the 25 sliding layers 0.002.
claims.hardware: RTX 5090, rented (Vast box 49785896)
claims.notes: Qwen3-30B control under the same model: -0.0006 nats. The kernel's own precision is flat in head dim on synthetic data (gnf4#324), so the cost is Gemma-4's activation statistics under 128-wide K groups at head_dim 512. SERVED (0.32.0 + grouped-nf4-gemm 0.26.0, 2026-09-04): per-layer groups (16 at D=512, 8 at D=256) move the paged path from 3.59239 to 3.57228 nats on the same window (-0.020; fp8 throughout); Qwen3-30B bit-exact at 1.61067 with its unchanged 4 groups.
claims.conditions: 512 scored steps, 256-token prompt, sha e01de6ebd4af; roundings applied on rows >= 256 (the paged prefill attends on bf16)

claims.claim: Two arithmetically equivalent forwards of an MoE model disagree because rounding flips router top-k choices: 4.52% of (layer, token) choices on gpt-oss-20b and 6.77% on Qwen3-30B, with the disagreement carried by the flipped tokens (KL 0.0504 vs 0.0013). Every parity delta must be read against a per-model measured floor, never against zero.
claims.unit: % of (layer, token) top-k choices that flip (gpt-oss)
claims.hardware: RTX 5090, rented
claims.notes: Floors: Granite 0.0033, Qwen3 0.0095, gpt-oss 0.0176 nats (512-step windows). Flip RATE does not predict floor SIZE.

claims.claim: RETIRED: 'the fp8 paged KV cache costs +0.047 ppl on Qwen3-30B and +0.022 on Granite against a bf16 cache'.
claims.retired_reason: The +0.047 ppl is +0.0058 nats, BELOW Qwen3's measured 0.0095-nat arithmetic-order floor; Granite's +0.0028 is below its 0.0033 floor. Indistinguishable from reordering the arithmetic; not attributable to the cache. The derived rule 'buy headroom back from the cache first' is retired with it.
quoted_in: CHANGELOG.md 0.30.0 (left as written; corrected by a Corrections entry)

claims.claim: RETIRED: 'gpt-oss's +0.078 nats is 10-20x every other family, a real signal about the sinks and sliding-window path'.
claims.retired_reason: Against a chunk-free reference the paged path sits at 0.00288 nats, below its floor; the chunked oracle it had been compared to is 6x further from the truth than the path. The 8192-step number tracked the oracle's 32 chunk boundaries, not the serving path.

claims.claim: RETIRED (mechanism only): 'chunked teacher-forced scoring is not equivalent to one full forward on a family whose layers alternate sliding and full attention'. The measurement stands; the attribution to sliding windows is refuted.
claims.retired_reason: Widening the window past the context leaves the gap at KL 0.0178; every cache class gives the same gap. The cause is MoE router flips (e4b.parity.moe-routing-flip-floor), which applies to every MoE model.

claims.claim: FALSIFIED as pre-registered: the KL gate for chat-only families (mean full-vocab KL <= 0.01 nats/token, top-1 >= 99%).
claims.retired_reason: Its first measurement rejects a shipped configuration (NF4 vs bf16 experts: 0.029 nats, 93.6% top-1). The 0.01 was calibrated from a signed NLL difference and applied to a full-vocabulary KL, a different and strictly larger quantity. Left textually unchanged in METHODOLOGY 13, marked falsified; not retuned.

claims.claim: e4b's gpt-oss expert path is faithful: MXFP4 dequant bit-identical to transformers' and to an independent decode; the NF4 expert forward matches HF's reference math at cosine 0.991-0.993; the served layer 0 inside the running model matches the reference MoE at cosine 0.998 per token.
claims.hardware: RTX 5090, rented

claims.claim: OPEN: Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it fails to load with 'CUDA error: invalid argument' on 2 of 4 rented 5090 hosts, inside load_moe_4bit_streaming after the experts quantise; the traceback site may not be the faulting kernel (asynchronous CUDA error).
claims.notes: A 2 GiB host-hop 'fix' was merged and reverted the same day (#350/#351): the model's largest tensor is 1.375 GiB, so it never triggered.

claims.claim: Full bf16 OLMoE-1B-7B (~13.9 GB) OOMs a 12 GB card; in 4-bit it loads at 4.70 GB and trains in under 8 GB, and the streaming loader never materialises the bf16 model in CPU or GPU RAM (verified under a 3 GB container RAM cap).
claims.hardware: RTX A2000 12 GB in a NAS PCIe 3.0 x8 slot

claims.claim: QLoRA on frozen NF4 experts improves a held-out Alpaca eval from 1.4813 to 1.0290 on OLMoE-1B-7B.
claims.notes: PROVENANCE.md is the OTS-anchored record for this v0.2.0 result specifically; later additions are receipted in bench/ and docs/, not in that file.

claims.claim: Adapter placement: experts+attention is the best eval (1.0268) and attention-only is the efficiency pick, reaching 92% of the achievable reduction at 2.1 M trainable params (3.5%); training the router hurts.

With OFFLOAD_EXPERTS=1 the frozen experts stream from pinned CPU RAM one layer at a time, so a fused MoE whose 4-bit experts exceed the card still QLoRA-trains on 12 GB: Qwen3-30B-A3B peaks at 7.16 GB and Gemma-4-26B-A4B at 8.47 GB, both of which OOM without offload. Cost is about +11% s/step at OLMoE scale.

Against a descending host-RAM cap the arena path completes where the host-RAM path does not: OLMoE 2.56x, Gemma-4 3.80x, Qwen3-30B 6.40x lower host-RAM requirement; at an 8.59 GB cap Qwen3-30B is OOM-killed on host RAM and trains to completion on the arena.
claims.notes: The load saving travels across architectures; the per-step cost does NOT and is worse on faster cards (an arena step includes an NVMe read). Quote the step cost with the card attached.

claims.claim: enable_fast_train(model, dgrad=True) is the fastest training lane at real width (2.52x on Qwen3-30B, 48 layers, A6000) while enable_batched_train wins only the toy microbench (24.01x at hidden 512) and gives no speedup at real width (1.05x) with the highest peak memory.
claims.notes: dgrad adds no composed gradient error over the lane it extends (4.97e-2 -> 4.99e-2); every lane including the reference sits on the composed bf16 noise floor.

claims.claim: Across two 30B-class MoEs (Qwen3-30B-A3B and Gemma-4-26B-A4B), five datasets each, 200 steps per cell: the fused training path runs 1.52-1.81x faster per step at 0.75-0.81x peak VRAM and 0.86-0.92x energy per step, with loss parity on both registered criteria (worst cell 0.03653 against a 0.05 band) and the frozen 4-bit stack verified bit-identical over 16.31 GB hashed.
claims.notes: The first prereg is unanchored, so its ten cells are `measured`, not `confirmed`; the model2 prereg says so explicitly and was stamped pre-data AND pre-hardware. Single same-process A/B per cell: ratios are indicative, not variance-bounded.

claims.claim: Choosing resident experts from a routing histogram rather than by index buys +56% (K=4) and +120% (K=8) decode on gpt-oss-20b at identical VRAM, +44% on Gemma-4-26B and +37.1% on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, where index-ordered was statistically indistinguishable from pure streaming.
claims.notes: The size of the gain is a property of the HOST: +40% on a thin-link A2000, about 0% on a fat-PCIe L40S. On an A6000 with a 128-expert model the informed cells did not replicate and were withdrawn as evidence.

claims.claim: DeepSeek-V4-Flash (43 layers x 256 experts, 284B) loads in about 10 s at 8.74 GiB peak VRAM and generates, with 147 GB of experts served from an on-disk arena.

capture_decode replays a decode step as one CUDA graph: 4.4-5.6x on 2-layer fixtures, 1.11x on real OLMoE weights and 1.04x on Qwen3-30B — the gain is inversely proportional to real GPU work per step. Both real-weight models replay bit-identical to eager.
claims.notes: Do not expect it to matter at 30B. StaticCache is allocated to max_length up front; step() is greedy argmax with no logits processors, which is why the HTTP server does not use it.

claims.claim: 4-bit vs bf16 on a card that already fits the model is a 1.2-2.3x ENERGY PENALTY (NF4 is storage-only, the GEMM runs in bf16 either way, plus dequant). It inverts when memory binds, where the freed memory unlocks a batch worth up to 4.4x lower energy per token.
claims.unit: x energy penalty when the model already fits

claims.claim: RESTATED: the registered 13.47x training speedup is about 7.2x against a current baseline.
claims.retired_reason: transformers v5 ships grouped_mm_experts_forward and fused the per-expert loop upstream, moving the baseline from 50.86 to 26.6 s/step. The grouped arm did not regress (3.77 -> 3.7). Roughly half the published multiple is now upstream's work. Restate as 7.2x over a current-transformers bnb baseline, same-box, with held-out eval parity.

claims.claim: OPEN: no shipped tool bakes the arena. TRAIN_ARENA takes a path to a pre-baked arena, is undocumented in train.py --help, and nvme_arena.bake_expert_tensors only RELOCATES pre-quantised tensors, so reproducing the TR2 training receipt from published artifacts requires writing a quantise-and-emit step yourself (~60 lines).
claims.notes: Also: passing a non-path truthy TRAIN_ARENA releases 16.31 GB of expert storage BEFORE discovering the arena is missing.

claims.claim: OPEN/DOWNGRADED: 'int8-offload posts the best training eval' is confounded. The audit found an evaluator offset (0.0026-0.0054) the same order as the placement gaps being claimed (0.0015-0.0108), and the bundle's consolidated CSV mislabels host for 6 of 12 repeat jobs.
SUPERSEDED: the v0 offload decode grid (OLMoE 1.44 tok/s at 1.68 GB; Gemma-4 0.43; Qwen3-30B 0.22).
claims.retired_reason: The pipelined and paged engines supersede these for decode. docs/INFERENCE.md declares this itself.
